title: Service Automation Credentials Journey + sketches
summary: Exploratory notes + wireframe text for a focused journey: teams provisioning credentials for automation (CI/CD, cron jobs, sync agents) with least-privilege defaults, rotation/exception handling, and audit-log surfaces.
content:
Context:
This is a working doc capturing UX thinking for a compact flow aimed at engineers and SREs who need to create non-human credentials for automation (service accounts, API keys, signed tokens). Goal is to reduce confusion between API keys vs service account keys, standardize rotation/expiry, and make audit signals obvious when keys are used by automated workloads.

High-level problems we see:
- Users create long-lived API keys for automation because the console makes it faster; rotation is manual and poorly visible.
- Service accounts are powerful but mapping them to specific CI/CD jobs is unclear.
- Teams want ephemeral credentials for pipelines but need simple integrations (GitHub Actions, GCP Workload Identity, self-hosted runners).
- Audit queries are hard: "which key was used by what run?" requires linking telemetry, not just log lines.

Design principles
- Default to least privilege: when creating credentials, show a compact policy preview with an estimated blast radius score (low/medium/high).
- Make rotation and TTL first-class: creation wizard includes expiry/auto-rotate toggles and recommended presets (7d, 30d, 90d).
- Provide a small surface for mapping to integrations (GitHub, Jenkins, Kubernetes) with templated examples to copy into workflows.
- Surface audit and usage: show recent uses (last 14d) and allow one-click investigation drilldown to request ids/region.
- Fail safely: deny creation of unrestricted keys unless explicit bypass with reason and reviewer.

Suggested flow (compact wizard)
1) Entry point: "Create automation credential" CTA on org/team credentials page. Option: API key | service account key (managed) | short-lived token
2) Step 1 - Intent + name
   - Name (required)
   - Intent dropdown (CI/CD, cron job, sync agent, third-party integration)
   - Optional: Attach to repository or pipeline (autocomplete)
3) Step 2 - Scope and permissions
   - Minimal role suggestions based on intent (learned heuristics + past samples)
   - Compact policy preview (human readable + JSON toggle)
   - Blast radius indicator (green/amber/red) with inline suggestions to reduce scope
4) Step 3 - Rotation & TTL
   - TTL presets (7d/30d/90d/none) with short guidance "choose shorter TTL for CI short-lived runs"
   - Auto-rotate toggle and who will be notified (team members)
   - Option: "Generate both short-lived token + persistent refresh key" pattern for specific integrations
5) Step 4 - Integration snippets
   - One-click copy for GitHub Actions, GitLab CI, Kubernetes secret manifest, curl example
   - Small note about storing secrets in vaults and recommended patterns
6) Step 5 - Review & create
   - Summary: name, intent, scope, TTL, integrations selected
   - Inline audit note: this credential will be visible in audit logs with usage metadata and request ids
   - Create button + optional immediate rotate button

Wireframe text (compact view)
- Header: "Create automation credential" with breadcrumb: Org > Team > Credentials > New
- Left column: Wizard steps vertically (compact icons)
- Center panel: Form fields as above; keep to 6–8 form inputs max per step
- Right rail: Preview pane showing policy summary, blast radius, recent similar credentials (if any), and "Suggested roles" algorithm explanation (how we chose them)

Audit & observability surfaces
- Credential detail page should show:
  - Last used (time) and top 10 callers (service names / IP ranges)
  - Event timeline: create, rotate, revoke, permission changes, and notable uses (failed auths, anomalous geo)
  - Quick actions: revoke, rotate, limit scope, add exception (requires reviewer)
- Searchability: allow filters by credential name, owner, intent tag, last used, TTL, scope levels
- Link from audit entry -> request detail page with request id, model invoked, route, tokens consumed, region, and originating credential id

Edge cases / policy exceptions
- Emergency credentials: allow creation of an unrestricted credential but require a reason and assign an automatic expiry (e.g., 24h) and optional postmortem requirement. Record reviewer afterwards.
- Cross-team delegation: allow "delegate by tag" where one team grants a consuming tag to another team; delegation flow should record approvals and a link to the owning team.
- Migration from legacy keys: bulk import CSV of key ids with auto-scan of usage; recommend TTLs and show suggested remediation plan.

Open questions / design tradeoffs
- How opinionated should role suggestions be? (risk: overconstraining new users vs benefit of fewer mis-scoped keys)
- Should we force short-lived tokens for first-party infra integrations (e.g., Redwood-managed runners)?
- How do we instrument "which key was used by what inference request" without leaking sensitive payloads? Need to coordinate with runtime to add credential id metadata into traces.
- Reviewer UX for exception approvals: Slack/Email integration? In-console reviewer queue?

Metrics & success criteria
- % of new automation credentials created with TTL <= 30d (target 75% after launch)
- Mean time to revoke compromised credential (target < 10m for automated revoke flows)
- Reduced number of "unscoped" credentials (blast radius red) created per week by 60%
- Usage of integration snippets (copy to clipboard events) as proxy for correct setup

Notes to self / next steps
- Build prototype screens in Figma (Evan) using the center + right-rail pattern. Include 3 sample intents with role suggestions.
- Backend: add credential_id to runtime request logs (Riley + infra) and sketch how it surfaces to trace UI.
- Product: define reviewer policy for exception flow and integrate with SSO groups (Mateo)
- PM to write a short migration playbook for teams with >10 legacy keys

References and tickets
- PLT-1427: backend schema for credential metadata (linked above)
- ORG-CONSOLE-328: audit query patterns and sample SQLs on telemetry store
- github:pull/874: initial console form controls PR (prototype)

Rough mock ascii (very rough)
[Create automation credential]  Step 1 / 5
Name: [ cron-sync-ec2 ]  Intent: [cron job v]
Scope: [Read-only embeddings index]  Policy preview: [read-only: embeddings.index]  Blast radius: [GREEN]
TTL: [30d v]  Auto-rotate: [x]
Integration snippets: [GitHub Action] [K8s Secret] [curl]

Unresolved
- Exact telemetry fields and retention for usage table (privacy concerns for request payloads)
- Whether to auto-suggest reviewers for exceptions from codeowners or team admins

End of doc.
